_comment: Evidence-based root-cause register for BELOW/odd findings. Keys are scenario names as they appear in metrics. compare.py merges these into the BELOW register of docs/COMPARATIVE-BENCHMARK.md. Every entry cites the run + artifact that produced it. Updated by bench forensics; never fabricated.

delete_partition.root_cause: lost::discover returns ONE candidate when TWO NTFS partitions were deleted: the deep tree carries only 'Candidate @ 32768' (668 rows = partition A; 0 rows for partition B / BENCH2). The og found BOTH partitions in the same state (rsf roots 'BENCH (NTFS)' 1213 rows + 'BENCH2 (NTFS)' 1183 rows). The raw-recall tie (ours 43.0% vs og 42.7%) is deceptive: ours is DISCOVERY-limited, og is CAP-limited (og Give-Up at 520.29 MB of 512 MiB quota while recovering partition A; B never attempted - the attempted-set normalization exposes it). Suspect: candidate A's extent covers partition B's boot-sector window (nested same-fs dedup) or the B-window probe is rejected by overlap scoring vs the live (empty) table.
delete_partition.fix_plan: Engine session: unit fixture with two deleted NTFS partitions at unequal offsets; debug lost::discover candidate enumeration + dedup/overlap scoring; the og's SearchDLL finds both (corpus reference).
delete_partition.evidence: run 40073093997: bench-ours-ntfs-delete_partition tree-deep.csv/tree-deep.json (Candidate @ 32768 only); bench-og-ntfs-delete_partition og-found.csv (BENCH + BENCH2 roots); og 30_cap_gate_candidate.png (VLM: 597 files / 520.29 MB / 27.0% completed)

permanent_delete.ours_precision_note: MetadataOnly 'Lost' copies (remnant/orphan reconstruction, no extents) are enqueued by recover-all and committed as zero-filled files (991 'salvaged' in run 40073093997) - they count as false positives against the manifest. The writer's Skip-policy zero-fill is designed for PARTIAL spans of real files; whole no-extent items produce full-size zero files.
permanent_delete.fix_plan: Engine session: decide the product behavior for MetadataOnly items (skip with 'nothing to recover' outcome vs current zero-fill commit); the og does not emit content for metadata-only entries.
permanent_delete.evidence: run 40073093997: report-deepcarve.json outcomes {done 758, salvaged 991, error 599}; tree-deepcarve.json Lost Files/t000.jpg rows origin=2 deleted=3 confidence=4 (MetadataOnly), extents null

quick_format.root_cause: CONFIRMED post-transport-fix (run 40079065019, full profile): ours' remnant scanner recovers NAMES ONLY after a quick format - 10093 of 10148 tree rows are Origin=Lost/Damaged/MetadataOnly (no extents); recovery yields 10013 ERR_TRUNCATED + 133 done + 1 salvaged = 0/10228 hash-true. The old MFT records survive the format as raw sectors (the remnant scan proves it finds them), but the $DATA runs are not being reconstructed/kept - the og's SearchDLL rebuilds full files from the same remnants (51.5% recall in the smoke measurement). This is the largest single recall gap: quick-format recovery is name-only for us.
quick_format.fix_plan: Engine session: cr_mftwalk remnant path - after a quick format the old MFT records (with their $DATA runlists) are intact raw sectors; parse the remnant records' runlists instead of downgrading to MetadataOnly. The og reference: NTFSSearchDLL remnant scan (corpus). Regression fixture: quick-formatted NTFS volume with known files.
quick_format.evidence: run 40079065019 bench-ours-ntfs-quick_format: metrics-*.json (0/10228 all modes), report-deepcarve.json ({done 133, error 10013, salvaged 1}), tree-deepcarve.json (10093 rows origin=2 deleted=3 conf=4); smoke comparison: og 51.5% (305/592)

behavior_probes.root_cause: resume-equivalence FAILS: the resumed scan's tree carries EXTRA carved entries the uninterrupted scan's tree does not (RESUME DIFF rows '=>' Carved000000.mkv / Carved000015.zip / Carved001026.zip etc.). Suspect: the carve dedup index (F9 extent-class) is not carried across the resume boundary, so the resumed carve re-emits extents the uninterrupted run suppressed - OR the post-resume carve pass sees a different dedup baseline from the restored tree. nodriver + cancel probes PASS (BENCH-F1 salvage proven: 1328 rows readable from the hard-killed checkpoint); this is the remaining red in ours-behavior.
behavior_probes.fix_plan: Engine session: capture_snapshot + resume path - verify the carve dedup index is restored from the session (or rebuilt from the loaded tree) before the resumed carve stage; regression test = the exact probe flow (kill at 6 s -> resume -> diff vs uninterrupted).
behavior_probes.evidence: runs 40073093997 + 40077233920 ours-behavior artifacts (behavior.json resume probe, RESUME DIFF samples); scripts in bench/ours/run-behavior.ps1 probe 3

fat32_deleted_recovery.root_cause: FAT32 deleted-file recovery is DOUBLY broken (run 40079065019 full matrix, all FAT32 volume-scan cells): (1) NAMES LOST - the tree emits 8.3 short names (SEED\\TINY\\_000.JPG for seed/tiny/t000.jpg); the deleted-LFN assembly does not reconstruct long names. (2) CONTENT WRONG - of 10143 files committed 'done' by the writer with SIZES matching the manifest, only 46 have manifest-matching SHA-256: the deleted-chain reconstruction points at the wrong clusters (the classic first-cluster-only problem: freed chains cannot be walked, and the current guess produces plausible-size, wrong-byte files). The disk-level path (delete_partition, 49.7%) works because the lost-partition engine re-reads the volume differently. exFAT on the same matrix: 99.94% recall / 99.16% precision.
fat32_deleted_recovery.fix_plan: Engine session: (a) deleted-LFN assembly for FAT32 (LFN entry pairs precede the 8.3 entry; both survive deletion - the exFAT path already does this); (b) deleted-chain reconstruction policy: do not emit confident chain guesses as recoverable content - grade them (the FREE-first-cluster honesty cap exists for exactly this) or validate against the carve layer.
fat32_deleted_recovery.evidence: run 40079065019 bench-ours-fat32-unlink_native: tree-deepcarve.csv (SEED\\TINY\\_000.JPG rows), report-deepcarve.json ({done 10143, error 150}), rematch via scripts/rematch_inventory.py (46/10143 hash-true); all FAT32 volume cells 0-0.3% recall vs exFAT 99.9%

refs_detection.root_cause: ReFS real-volume support is effectively absent: every ReFS volume-scan cell returns rc=0x50030001 (ERR_BAD_MAGIC) in ~2 ms with 0 files - the ReFS boot-sector/detection path rejects real Windows Server 2022 ReFS volumes outright (synthetic fixtures pass in tests; the real on-disk layout - ReFS 3.7 - is refused). All 11 ReFS volume cells recall 0.0%.
refs_detection.fix_plan: Engine session: dump a real Server-2022 ReFS boot sector from the run artifacts (hashmap-pre.csv proves the volume existed), compare against detect_refs' expected layout, fix the probe. The og ships ReFSSearchDLL (corpus) - run B measures its ReFS coverage for the comparison.
refs_detection.evidence: run 40079065019 bench-ours-refs-* stage logs: 'scan end rc=0x50030001 files=0 ... elapsed_ms=2' on every ReFS cell

ntfs_decay_grading.root_cause: NTFS recall collapses non-linearly under sector-reuse decay: decay_50 = 96.4% but decay_80 = 0.2% (20/10216) - while exFAT holds 98.6% at decay_80. The NTFS $Bitmap viability grading (Excellent/Overwritten classes) drops content when extents are marked reused, whereas the exFAT path keeps partial content. The og's behavior at decay_80 (run B) decides whether this is a parity gap or an ours-only collapse.
ntfs_decay_grading.fix_plan: Engine session: revisit the R2.4 viability-to-emission mapping on NTFS - Overwritten files should still emit their unreused extents as PartialRisk content (the corpus og keeps partials), not be dropped to metadata-only.
ntfs_decay_grading.evidence: run 40079065019: bench-ours-ntfs-decay_80 metrics (0.2% vs decay_50 96.4%) vs bench-ours-exfat-decay_80 (98.6%)
